content.text: {"answer":"The supplied results do not directly address a topic specifically called “Than fairness limits.” [1]-[10] instead discuss fairness limits in different technical settings (e.g., fundamental impossibility trade-offs, constraints from limited capacity, or verification/streaming/group fairness). [1] is the closest to “fairness limits” in a general, theory-impossibility sense, arguing for intrinsic trade-offs between fairness and performance and limits from finite samples and model expressivity. [3] discusses practical limits under hard resource constraints that can dominate ethical priorities, and [6] addresses limits of fairness verification by developing quantitative bounds for tree ensembles.\n\nIf you meant “limits” more specifically as theoretical impossibility, [1] provides “No-Free-Fairness” results covering irreducible subgroup costs, finite-sample effects, statistical bottlenecks from strict fairness, and model-class expressivity constraints. [2] and [9] focus more on how to optimize across competing fairness notions, while [3] focuses on operational constraints (single global thresholds) and [4] on fairness under strategic classification via randomized thresholds. [8] studies how fairness-driven exploration in recommenders can saturate and vary across users.","grounded":false}
